tools.name: open_template_gallery
tools.title: Open template gallery
tools.summary: Browse your templates in a visual gallery, filterable by channel, status, language and type.
tools.description:
Browse the user's templates in a visual gallery, all connected
channels by default. To show ONE template the user already named, call
preview_template instead (each tool renders its own panel).
Pass a filter ONLY when the user asked for it: "list my templates" takes
none. Each one silently hides the rest -- type hides every other format,
status hides every other review state -- so an unrequested pair returns
an empty gallery that reads as an empty account.
(SMS channel only: the DLT gateway reports ENABLED/DISABLED, which this
tool maps onto APPROVED/REJECTED for the shared filter. WhatsApp always
uses real APPROVED/PENDING/REJECTED -- never say Enabled for WhatsApp.)

status.description: Omit for any listing: the unfiltered gallery already shows every template with its status badge (approved, pending, rejected). NEVER call once per status to summarise -- read the badges from one call instead. Pass a status only when the user asked for that review state ('show my pending templates').

name.description: EXACT template name to find (e.g. 'rakshabandhan'). Matched with ==, so a label or phrase like 'RCS carousel templates' will NEVER match anything — omit unless the user said a template name.

language.description: Exact language code as stored on the template (e.g. 'en', 'en_US' — these do not cross-match). Omit unless the user asked for a language.

type.description: Omit for any listing: ONE call already returns every format (text, image, video, document, carousel) merged in a single gallery. NEVER call this tool once per type to 'list all' -- that renders duplicate panels. Pass a type only when the user asked for that format by name ('show my carousel templates').

limit.description: Pass ONLY when the user themselves said a number ('show my 5 templates' -> 5). Omit otherwise -- the gallery already shows everything, newest first. Words like 'latest', 'top' or 'all' are NOT a limit.

offset.description: Never pass this on your own. Page through results only when the user explicitly asks for the next page.

tools.name: preview_template
tools.title: Draft or preview a template
tools.summary: Draft new template copy (including 2-6 A/B options) or preview an existing template, rendered as it appears on the phone.
tools.description:
Draft new template copy or preview an existing template, rendered
visually. Any request to draft/write/compose a template is THIS tool,
not a chat answer. Existing: pass name or template_id
(template_id for SMS -- DLT names aren't unique; ids are strings).
New copy: pass draft instead (one content object, or 2-6 for A/B
options; name/category then label the draft). Build the draft only
from what the user asked for: map each piece of their content to its
correct component, never add a component (header, footer, buttons)
they did not request, and never move content between components. If a
request fits no component (e.g. a button that sends a reply message),
say so and offer what exists (URL or Call button) instead of adapting
it. Drafts: ONE call with
channel omitted previews every connected channel in one panel --
NEVER call once per channel; pass channel only when the user names
one. Preview only, nothing is saved; after the user confirms, pass
the SAME content object to save_template.
WhatsApp category -> type (honour the ones the user names, else pick
both from the use case): AUTHENTICATION = TEXT only, drafted as
{"type": "AUTHENTICATION", "otp": {...}}; MARKETING = TEXT, media,
CAROUSEL, LIMITED_TIME_OFFER (optional IMAGE/VIDEO header; COPY_CODE
button required when the offer expires), and the only category taking
a COPY_CODE button; UTILITY = TEXT, media, CAROUSEL, no
LIMITED_TIME_OFFER. Media formats: IMAGE, VIDEO, DOCUMENT, LOCATION, and
GIF (MARKETING only, supplied as an MP4 file).
MM WA Pay, Order Details and Order Status do not exist yet -- say so
rather than substituting a TEXT template.

AuthContent.description: Meta controls the body text. Use with category AUTHENTICATION.

Body.description: Message body text plus example values for its placeholders.

text.description: Body copy. At most 1024 characters. The body may use *bold* and emojis; headers and button labels may not. Variable syntax differs by channel: WhatsApp uses numbered {{1}}, {{2}}; RCS uses NAMED placeholders in square brackets, [ORDER_ID], [DELIVERY_DATE] -- the RCS send API fills customParams keyed by name, so a numbered placeholder in an RCS body is delivered as literal text. (SMS/DLT uses {#var#}.)

examples.description: One example per {{n}} placeholder, in order. Required at save time for WhatsApp. Not used for RCS, whose [NAMED] variables are supplied per send instead.

Button.description: One template button / RCS suggestion chip.

text.description: Label; required for every type EXCEPT COPY_CODE, where it must be omitted -- WhatsApp renders its own label there. No newlines, emojis, or formatting characters. A Quick Reply button is a label only -- it sends no reply message back to the user.

value.description: The button's target, per type: the URL for URL, the phone number for PHONE_NUMBER, the offer code for COPY_CODE. On RCS it is also the postback for QUICK_REPLY / SHARE_LOCATION / CALENDAR_EVENT -- the string your bot RECEIVES when the chip is tapped. Set it whenever two chips could share a label: three carousel cards all labelled "Browse" are indistinguishable without it. Defaults to the label.

example.description: The offer code on a COPY_CODE button, or the sample for a dynamic {{n}} URL. That sample is the COMPLETE filled URL, not just the value of the placeholder: for value "https://x.com/order/{{1}}" pass "https://x.com/order/order123", never "order123". It must also differ from value -- Meta rejects a sample identical to the actual URL.

event_title.description: CALENDAR_EVENT only. The name of the entry saved to the recipient's calendar -- the EVENT's name, not the button label. A chip labelled "Add to calendar" should carry event_title "Diwali Sale Preview".

event_description.description: CALENDAR_EVENT only. Notes on the calendar entry, e.g. the venue.

event_start.description: CALENDAR_EVENT only, REQUIRED. Either a fixed ISO 8601 start ("2026-08-22T18:00:00Z") or a named variable ("[EVENT_START]") filled per send via customParams -- the create API accepts both. What it cannot be is empty: there would be nothing to substitute into, and the chip opens an empty, untitled calendar entry.

event_end.description: CALENDAR_EVENT only, REQUIRED. ISO 8601 end ("2026-08-22T20:00:00Z") or a named variable ("[EVENT_END]").

url_type.description: URL buttons only, WhatsApp only. Leave unset and the type is inferred from value: STATIC, or DYNAMIC when it holds a {{n}} placeholder. Set DYNAMIC_LINK_TRACK to send the link through Gupshup's click-tracking redirect, where value is the tracking base (e.g. "https://m.gs.im/e") and needs no placeholder or example.

buttons.description: WhatsApp: up to 2 per card. RCS: up to 4 suggestions per card. Every card needs at least one, and all cards must share the same button structure (Meta rule).

CarouselContent.description:
2-10 cards. RCS: media.url per card. WhatsApp: media.url / data / handle per card
(url or data is uploaded server-side to mint the Meta handle). Every card needs at
least one button, and all cards must share the same button structure (Meta rule).

body.description: The message shown ABOVE the cards, in its own bubble -- the intro copy, not a repeat of a card. Write it whenever the carousel needs one; left out, the first card's own text is reused for it, which renders the same sentence twice.

card_height.description: RCS only. Card height, default SHORT. With card_width this fixes the required image ratio: SHORT+SMALL 5:4 (960x720), SHORT+MEDIUM 2:1 (1440x720), MEDIUM+SMALL 4:5 (576x720), MEDIUM+MEDIUM 4:3 (1440x1080).

card_width.description: RCS only. Card width, default SMALL. See card_height.

LimitedTimeOfferContent.description:
A countdown-offer template. Needs at least one URL button; a COPY_CODE
button (max 1) leads the button list when present, and is mandatory when
the offer expires.

media_type.description: Optional header media. The console offers None/Image/Video only -- no document, no GIF. Must be set together with media, and named rather than inferred: guessing from the URL defaults an extension-less link to IMAGE, which renders a video in an .

LocationContent.description:
A map-pin header template -- one of the five MEDIA formats. It carries no
media object: the pin itself is supplied per message at send time.

buttons.description: WhatsApp: up to 10 (up to 10 quick replies, at most 2 URL and 1 phone button). RCS: up to 11 suggestion chips. Note 4+ buttons do not render in full on WhatsApp Desktop -- recipients are prompted to open the chat on their phone.

Media.description: Template media, from exactly one source: url, data, or handle.

url.description: Hosted media link (https, publicly reachable). WhatsApp accepts JPEG/PNG images up to 5 MB, MP4/3GPP video up to 16 MB, and PDF documents up to 100 MB. WebP, GIF, HEIC and AVIF files are refused -- convert to PNG/JPEG, or to MP4 for an animation.

data.description: Directly-attached file (base64). WhatsApp only. Same formats as url, but capped at 17 MB whatever the format -- a bigger file has to be hosted and passed as url instead.

handle.description: Meta media handle id for a carousel card. Optional — if you pass url or data instead, the server uploads it and mints the handle for you.

MediaContent.description:
A media-header template. GIF is MARKETING-only and its file is an MP4
(the console button reads "Choose GIF File (MP4 format)") -- a real .gif is
rejected at upload, so hand it the animation already converted.

buttons.description: WhatsApp: up to 10 (up to 10 quick replies, at most 2 URL and 1 phone button). RCS: up to 11 suggestion chips. Note 4+ buttons do not render in full on WhatsApp Desktop -- recipients are prompted to open the chat on their phone.

card_title.description: RCS only, REQUIRED: the rich card's headline, above the body. Without it the card is titled with the template's internal name (recipients read "rcs_offer_promo"). Ignored on WhatsApp.

card_orientation.description: RCS only. Card layout, default VERTICAL. Sets the media's required aspect ratio: VERTICAL+SHORT 3:1, VERTICAL+MEDIUM 2:1, HORIZONTAL 3:4.

card_height.description: RCS only. Media height on the card, default SHORT.

text.description: The offer banner line, at most 16 characters (e.g. "20% off today").

has_expiration.description: Draws the countdown strip. An expiring offer also REQUIRES a COPY_CODE button in buttons; without one the Gateway rejects the template.

expiration_ms.description: Only flips has_expiration on. The template itself carries no expiry date -- the Gateway's limited_time_offer payload has just text and has_expiration -- so the actual countdown deadline is supplied per message at send time, not here.

button_text.description: The copy-code button caption. Meta only accepts "Copy code" here (case-insensitive) and rejects any other wording, so there is nothing to choose -- leave it unset. To name the AUTOFILL button on a ONE_TAP/ZERO_TAP template, use autofill_text, which is free text.

otp_type.description: How the code reaches the app, mirroring the console's Code delivery radio. COPY_CODE: the customer copies and pastes it, quickest to set up. ONE_TAP: tapping sends it straight to the app. ZERO_TAP: it fills in with no tap at all. Both tap modes render an autofill button AND a copy-code fallback, and both need the app identifiers below.

autofill_text.description: ONE_TAP only, required. The autofill button caption, e.g. "Autofill".

package_name.description: ONE_TAP/ZERO_TAP only, required. The Android package name of the app that receives the code, e.g. "com.example.app". Ask the user for it -- it cannot be guessed from the brand.

signature_hash.description: ONE_TAP/ZERO_TAP only, required. The app's signing-key hash, exactly 11 characters (the console field counts 0/11). Ask the user for it; it comes from their Android build.

zero_tap_terms_accepted.description: ZERO_TAP only, required and must be true. The console makes the user tick a WhatsApp Business Terms acknowledgement before zero-tap can be turned on, so the caller has to confirm the same thing here -- do not set it on the user's behalf without asking.

card_title.description: Not valid here. A text message has no card, so it has no headline -- card_title belongs to an RCS rich card (type IMAGE or VIDEO).

header.description: Short text line, e.g. 'Order update'. Not a URL. No newlines, emojis, or formatting characters.

buttons.description: WhatsApp: up to 10 (up to 10 quick replies, at most 2 URL and 1 phone button). RCS: up to 11 suggestion chips. Note 4+ buttons do not render in full on WhatsApp Desktop -- recipients are prompted to open the chat on their phone.

tools.summary: Create or update a WhatsApp or RCS template and submit it for approval, after you confirm the preview.

template and submit it for review. Use only after the user confirms a
preview_template draft -- pass the identical content object; updates
replace the template, so re-pass media/footer/buttons to keep them.

different name -- the first attempt may have succeeded.

SaveOptions.description: Advanced save_template switches; defaults are right for almost all saves.

card_title.description: Not valid here. A text message has no card, so it has no headline -- card_title belongs to an RCS rich card (type IMAGE or VIDEO).

header.description: Short text line, e.g. 'Order update'. Not a URL. No newlines, emojis, or formatting characters.

buttons.description: WhatsApp: up to 10 (up to 10 quick replies, at most 2 URL and 1 phone button). RCS: up to 11 suggestion chips. Note 4+ buttons do not render in full on WhatsApp Desktop -- recipients are prompted to open the chat on their phone.

tools.name: preview_multilingual_templates
tools.title: Preview multilingual templates (WhatsApp)
tools.summary: Preview one WhatsApp template in several languages side by side (11 Indian languages plus English).
tools.description:
One WhatsApp template family in several languages, previewed TOGETHER
in a single panel — shown ONCE. Use whenever the user wants the same
template in 2+ languages (multilingual / translate / localize /
regional languages); single-language work stays with preview_template.
Same name for every language; supply each language's translated content
(en, hi, bn, gu, kn, ml, mr, pa, ta, te, ur). If the user gave no name,
suggest one from the content and show it here for confirmation. A
localized "Change Language" quick reply is added to every variant
automatically — do NOT add one yourself. The validated family is FROZEN
server-side under the returned draft_id: to submit, call
create_multilingual_templates with just that draft_id (never re-send
the content — what was previewed is exactly what ships). Submit only
after the user's explicit yes. Do NOT call this tool again for the same
family — not to 'confirm', not before submitting, not after creating.
Show the panel once, then submit or relay the create report as text.

AuthContent.description: Meta controls the body text. Use with category AUTHENTICATION.

Body.description: Message body text plus example values for its placeholders.

text.description: Body copy. At most 1024 characters. The body may use *bold* and emojis; headers and button labels may not. Variable syntax differs by channel: WhatsApp uses numbered {{1}}, {{2}}; RCS uses NAMED placeholders in square brackets, [ORDER_ID], [DELIVERY_DATE] -- the RCS send API fills customParams keyed by name, so a numbered placeholder in an RCS body is delivered as literal text. (SMS/DLT uses {#var#}.)

examples.description: One example per {{n}} placeholder, in order. Required at save time for WhatsApp. Not used for RCS, whose [NAMED] variables are supplied per send instead.

Button.description: One template button / RCS suggestion chip.

text.description: Label; required for every type EXCEPT COPY_CODE, where it must be omitted -- WhatsApp renders its own label there. No newlines, emojis, or formatting characters. A Quick Reply button is a label only -- it sends no reply message back to the user.

value.description: The button's target, per type: the URL for URL, the phone number for PHONE_NUMBER, the offer code for COPY_CODE. On RCS it is also the postback for QUICK_REPLY / SHARE_LOCATION / CALENDAR_EVENT -- the string your bot RECEIVES when the chip is tapped. Set it whenever two chips could share a label: three carousel cards all labelled "Browse" are indistinguishable without it. Defaults to the label.

example.description: The offer code on a COPY_CODE button, or the sample for a dynamic {{n}} URL. That sample is the COMPLETE filled URL, not just the value of the placeholder: for value "https://x.com/order/{{1}}" pass "https://x.com/order/order123", never "order123". It must also differ from value -- Meta rejects a sample identical to the actual URL.

event_title.description: CALENDAR_EVENT only. The name of the entry saved to the recipient's calendar -- the EVENT's name, not the button label. A chip labelled "Add to calendar" should carry event_title "Diwali Sale Preview".

event_description.description: CALENDAR_EVENT only. Notes on the calendar entry, e.g. the venue.

event_start.description: CALENDAR_EVENT only, REQUIRED. Either a fixed ISO 8601 start ("2026-08-22T18:00:00Z") or a named variable ("[EVENT_START]") filled per send via customParams -- the create API accepts both. What it cannot be is empty: there would be nothing to substitute into, and the chip opens an empty, untitled calendar entry.

event_end.description: CALENDAR_EVENT only, REQUIRED. ISO 8601 end ("2026-08-22T20:00:00Z") or a named variable ("[EVENT_END]").

url_type.description: URL buttons only, WhatsApp only. Leave unset and the type is inferred from value: STATIC, or DYNAMIC when it holds a {{n}} placeholder. Set DYNAMIC_LINK_TRACK to send the link through Gupshup's click-tracking redirect, where value is the tracking base (e.g. "https://m.gs.im/e") and needs no placeholder or example.

buttons.description: WhatsApp: up to 2 per card. RCS: up to 4 suggestions per card. Every card needs at least one, and all cards must share the same button structure (Meta rule).

CarouselContent.description:
2-10 cards. RCS: media.url per card. WhatsApp: media.url / data / handle per card
(url or data is uploaded server-side to mint the Meta handle). Every card needs at
least one button, and all cards must share the same button structure (Meta rule).

body.description: The message shown ABOVE the cards, in its own bubble -- the intro copy, not a repeat of a card. Write it whenever the carousel needs one; left out, the first card's own text is reused for it, which renders the same sentence twice.

card_height.description: RCS only. Card height, default SHORT. With card_width this fixes the required image ratio: SHORT+SMALL 5:4 (960x720), SHORT+MEDIUM 2:1 (1440x720), MEDIUM+SMALL 4:5 (576x720), MEDIUM+MEDIUM 4:3 (1440x1080).

card_width.description: RCS only. Card width, default SMALL. See card_height.

LimitedTimeOfferContent.description:
A countdown-offer template. Needs at least one URL button; a COPY_CODE
button (max 1) leads the button list when present, and is mandatory when
the offer expires.

media_type.description: Optional header media. The console offers None/Image/Video only -- no document, no GIF. Must be set together with media, and named rather than inferred: guessing from the URL defaults an extension-less link to IMAGE, which renders a video in an .

LocationContent.description:
A map-pin header template -- one of the five MEDIA formats. It carries no
media object: the pin itself is supplied per message at send time.

buttons.description: WhatsApp: up to 10 (up to 10 quick replies, at most 2 URL and 1 phone button). RCS: up to 11 suggestion chips. Note 4+ buttons do not render in full on WhatsApp Desktop -- recipients are prompted to open the chat on their phone.

Media.description: Template media, from exactly one source: url, data, or handle.

url.description: Hosted media link (https, publicly reachable). WhatsApp accepts JPEG/PNG images up to 5 MB, MP4/3GPP video up to 16 MB, and PDF documents up to 100 MB. WebP, GIF, HEIC and AVIF files are refused -- convert to PNG/JPEG, or to MP4 for an animation.

data.description: Directly-attached file (base64). WhatsApp only. Same formats as url, but capped at 17 MB whatever the format -- a bigger file has to be hosted and passed as url instead.

handle.description: Meta media handle id for a carousel card. Optional — if you pass url or data instead, the server uploads it and mints the handle for you.

MediaContent.description:
A media-header template. GIF is MARKETING-only and its file is an MP4
(the console button reads "Choose GIF File (MP4 format)") -- a real .gif is
rejected at upload, so hand it the animation already converted.

show_again.description: Leave FALSE. The preview panel is shown ONCE per family; calling this tool again for the same content returns a short reminder, not another panel. Set TRUE only when the user EXPLICITLY asks to see the preview again ('show me the preview again').

tools.name: create_multilingual_templates
tools.title: Create multilingual templates (WhatsApp)
tools.summary: Submit the exact multilingual family you previewed for Meta approval, after your explicit yes.
tools.description:
Submit a previewed multilingual family for Meta approval — call ONLY
after the user's explicit yes. Pass the SAME family you previewed:
name, category and variants (exactly like save_template for single
templates). You do NOT need a draft_id and you do NOT need to re-run
the preview to get one — the server matches your content to the draft
the user already reviewed and submits that frozen copy, so what was
previewed is exactly what ships. Only content that was actually
previewed can be submitted. Languages that already exist upstream are
skipped, so re-running after a partial failure creates only the missing
ones. Returns a per-language report (name, language, content, status) —
show it to the user in full as plain text; do not preview again.

tools.name: save_sms_dlt_template
tools.title: Save DLT template (SMS)
tools.summary: Register an already DLT-approved SMS template with Gupshup (asks for confirmation first).
tools.description:
Mirror an already telecom-DLT-approved SMS template into Gupshup
(nothing is submitted for approval; body must exactly match the
DLT-approved wording, variables as {#var#} or @__123__@).
Create: dlt_template_id, name, body, msg_type (TEXT for GSM/ASCII,
UNICODE_TEXT otherwise -- infer, don't ask), dlt_msg_type (must match
the account type), default_mask (sender id), category_id (-1 for any
transactional class without asking; ask only for PROMOTIONAL).
Update: template_id plus only the fields that change; dlt_template_id
can't change. First call returns a warning to relay; re-call with
user_confirmed=true after an explicit yes.

tools.name: get_template
tools.title: Get template details (WhatsApp, RCS)
tools.summary: The full structure of one template as data: body, variables, header, footer and buttons.
tools.description:
The full structure of ONE existing template as data: body and its
variables, header, footer, and every button (type, label, link). Use
this to answer structural questions about a template the user already has
-- does it have buttons or a QR button, what variables, what header --
without rendering a preview. For the on-phone visual use preview_template;
for only the approval verdict use get_template_status.

tools.name: get_template_status
tools.title: Check review status (WhatsApp, RCS)
tools.summary: Approval status of a WhatsApp or RCS template, with the rejection reason if rejected.
tools.description:
Review status (PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED + rejection reason) of a
WhatsApp or RCS template, by name or template_id. SMS has no review
step -- use open_template_gallery with channel sms instead.

tools.name: delete_template
tools.title: Delete template
tools.summary: Delete an SMS template (asks for confirmation first). WhatsApp and RCS templates are deleted from the Gupshup console.
tools.description:
SMS templates only. Do NOT call this tool for WhatsApp or RCS: they
have no working delete (upstream limitation, verified live), so answer
the user directly that the template cannot be deleted here and has to
be removed from the Gupshup console. SMS: pass template_id (DLT names
aren't unique; the DLT-portal approval itself is untouched). First call
returns a warning to relay; re-call with user_confirmed=true after an
explicit yes.

tools.name: preview_audience
tools.summary: Quick look at an audience: count, columns and a masked sample. Nothing is saved.
tools.description:
Cheap audience peek — count, columns, masked sample only (no persist, no ap:{id}).

Use to sanity-check a segment or file before review. For the normal send path pass the spec
to open_campaign_review directly instead of calling resolve_audience first.

audience_handle.description: Audience source to peek without persisting: cdp:all/segment, hubspot:all, hubspot:list:{id}, https URL, file path, or JSON. Bounded CRM preview only — no ap:{id}, no full pull.
audience_handle.title: Audience Handle

tools.name: get_cdp_summary
tools.summary: Size of your customer data and the fields you can segment on, with value counts.
tools.description:
Inspect the CDP audience before segmenting — sizes plus segmentable fields and their values.

Use when: user wants to target a segment (e.g. "at-risk customers", "high-value repeat buyers")
and you need to know which fields/values exist before calling resolve_audience with a cdp: filter.
Returns: total, opted_out, sendable, and segmentable_fields (each low-cardinality field mapped to
its distinct values with counts). Build a segment handle from these, e.g. cdp:churn_risk=at_risk,
then resolve_audience(cdp:...) → launch_campaign. Read-only.

tools.name: clear_cdp_data
tools.summary: Permanently delete all customer-data profiles for the account. Irreversible; requires explicit confirmation.
tools.description:
Permanently delete ALL CDP profiles for this account (uploaded contacts and CRM mirrors).

DESTRUCTIVE and irreversible. Before calling: tell the user what will be deleted (use
get_cdp_summary for the count) and get an explicit yes. Call with confirm=true only then.
Does not touch campaign history or analytics; a fresh CRM resolve or upload repopulates the CDP.

confirm.description: Must be true. Only set after the user has explicitly confirmed deletion in chat.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: resolve_audience
tools.summary: Save an audience server-side and get a handle for advanced sends and re-sends.
tools.description:
Persist audience server-side; return ap:{id}, count, columns, masked sample.

Use for advanced/direct sends, re-sends, or when you need ap:{id} before launch. For new
campaigns use open_campaign_review with the spec instead — full pull runs on panel Launch.
empty_segment returns segmentable_fields for retry. connector_error detail is safe to relay.

audience_handle.description: Audience source: cdp:all, cdp:segment (field<op>value; | OR, & AND), hubspot:all, hubspot:list:{id}, export URL, file, or JSON. Returns ap:{id}. See get_cdp_summary for segment fields.
audience_handle.title: Audience Handle

tools.name: launch_campaign
tools.summary: Send or schedule a campaign on WhatsApp, RCS or SMS, for clones, re-sends and advanced flows. New campaigns go through the review panel.
tools.description:
Send or schedule a campaign (whatsapp, rcs, or sms) from ap:{id}. Returns
campaign_id, status, recipients, follow_up_waves.

Use for clones, re-sends, and advanced flows — not new campaigns (open_campaign_review launches
via the panel). Background send when run_now; follow-up waves auto-fire.

audience_handle.description: Resolved handle from resolve_audience, format ap:{numeric_id}. Required.
audience_handle.title: Audience Handle

template_id.description: Approved template id/code from Template MCP as a STRING — always quote it, even when purely numeric (e.g. "8652536", never the bare number 8652536). REQUIRED for RCS; optional for WhatsApp. For SMS this is the Gupshup DLT lookup id — pass it to auto-fetch the approved DLT template text and its real dltTemplateId/principalEntityId (see send_options).
template_id.title: Template Id

template_body.description: Approved template text with variables (e.g. Hi {{first_name}}). Required for live WhatsApp bulk send; SMS sends it as the plain message text. Becomes the Gateway API msg field. When only template_id is known, leave this empty — the server fetches the approved body from the Gateway API automatically; never ask the user to paste it.
template_body.title: Template Body

tools.name: open_ab_test_review
tools.summary: Open the A/B test review panel: variants side by side, test on a sample, then send the winner to everyone else automatically.
tools.description:
REQUIRED for any A/B or split test of campaign copy/channels — never launch variants
yourself via launch_campaign directly.

Opens a pre-flight review panel showing each variant's bubble side by side with the shared
audience, then on Launch sends the test to a SAMPLE of the audience: 10% by default, at
most 1000 recipients, dealt evenly across the variants by hash(msisdn) so cohorts never
overlap and a retried launch reproduces the same split. Everyone else is held out. After
evaluate_after_hours (default 24) the server reads Gupshup's campaign stats for each
variant, picks the winner (click rate when any variant registered clicks, otherwise read
rate) and sends the winning template to the held-out recipients automatically -- nothing
for the agent or the user to do. get_campaign_status(logical id or any variant campaign
id) reports the test's state: testing (and when it is judged), promoted (winner, metric,
the holdout campaign), inconclusive, or failed. A file that already carries a template_id
column keeps its own mapping: the whole audience is the test and nothing is promoted.
Returns (structuredContent): review_session_id, count, recipient_count, variants (each with
its own recipient_count), ab_plan (mode, sample_size, holdout_count, evaluate_after_hours),
resolution ("immediate" | "at_launch"), launch_gate.

Pass the template_id the user named and leave template_body empty — the server fetches the approved body. Each variant needs a template_id or a template_body. Variants may vary copy and/or channel (whatsapp, rcs, sms); RCS variants require template_id. The audience needs only a PHONE column (plus %Var1..N when the templates have placeholders) — the server splits it and maps every recipient to its variant's template_id itself.
